label: attack-24-economics_attacker
system:
You are one member of a red team. You have been given ONE attack surface and you may not stray from it. You have not seen the author's reasoning and you do not want to; you see only the idea and the evidence.

Your job is to kill the idea on your surface. A weak attack wastes everyone's time. If your surface genuinely does not apply, say so with verdict "abstain" rather than inventing a weak objection; an abstention is not a survival.

Output JSON only.
user:
YOUR SURFACE — economics_attacker:
The margin or the acquisition cost never works. Use the real numbers: iOS cost per install $5.84, cost per paying user $20-$80, median revenue per payer $8-$24 monthly.

IDEA
{
  "id": 24,
  "title": "Sunday Post",
  "unlock": "A million-token context at flat pricing with cached input at roughly a 90% discount, on top of $0.10/M input text, means a whole family's accumulated photo captions and messages can be assembled into a weekly briefing for a fraction of a penny, with no retrieval pipeline to build.",
  "pain": "Family-connection products built around a box or a feed have died on hardware and on incumbents rather than on lack of feeling - Amazon Glow was discontinued within roughly a year on poor sales as a hardware product for a moment that passed [49], and Huxe shut down the day after Spotify shipped a near-identical personal feed feature [52].",
  "audience": "Grandparents over 70 living more than 200 miles from grandchildren they see a few times a year",
  "mechanic": "scheduled_digest",
  "wedge": "One page every Sunday at six: three photographs the parents already shared this week, written up in plain sentences naming each child, and three questions to ask on the phone.",
  "moat": "content_library",
  "model": "subscription",
  "loop": "gift_to_recipient",
  "kill": [
    "fewer than 35% of recipients open 4 consecutive weekly editions",
    "parents supply fewer than 5 photos in a week in more than half of households by week 6",
    "fewer than 15% of gift recipients or their families convert to a paying sender within 90 days",
    "fewer than 1 in 4 recipients report using the questions on an actual phone call in the first 200 surveyed"
  ],
  "why_not_obvious": "The obvious suggestion for distant grandparents is another video-calling device, which is exactly the shape of product that has already been discontinued [49], while the unmet part is not the call itself but having something specific to say on it.",
  "why_now": "The prepared briefing at a fixed hour is an old, working format, and holding a family's whole year of captions and messages in context to write one now costs under a penny a week with cached input [5][3], where it previously meant a retrieval pipeline and a vector database."
}



Return JSON:
{
  "surface": "economics_attacker",
  "attack": "your strongest specific argument, 2-4 sentences, concrete",
  "strongest_defence": "the best answer the author could give",
  "verdict": "fatal" | "wounded" | "survived" | "abstain",
  "verdict_reason": "one sentence"
}

Use "fatal" only when the defence cannot work at all, because a fatal verdict
kills the idea outright and no other score overrides it. Use "wounded" when the
idea survives but is materially weaker. Use "survived" when your surface is
genuinely well answered.
